title: OpenAI's New Reasoning Technique Alarms AI Safety Experts
content:
OpenAI's New Reasoning Technique Alarms AI Safety Experts 43
			
		 	
				An anonymous reader quotes a report from TechCrunch: OpenAI's new Astra model will use a reasoning technique called "recurrent depth" that allows it to operate outside of the sequential thinking that characterizes most reasoning models, The Information reported on Tuesday. This technique, also called "opaque recurrence," will likely make the model's chain of thought more difficult to monitor -- and that has AI safety experts rattled. While Astra's use of the technique is reportedly limited, its emergence has still raised significant concerns among AI safety experts.
 
"I am extremely concerned by the reporting that Astra uses opaque recurrence," wrote Redwood CEO Buck Shlegeris in a post after the news broke. "I don't know whether Astra is much less CoT monitorable than previous models. But if OpenAI pushes this technique further, they'll have the option to massively increase the recurrence and totally destroys CoT monitorability."
 
Longtime AI safety advocate Zvi Mowshowitz also weighed in and wrote that laws might be necessary to prevent a "race to the bottom" among AI labs. "The technique is playing with fire, risking a taboo that OpenAI and Anthropic have fought to establish that we work hard to maintain Chain of Thought faithfulness and monitorability for as long as we can," Mowshowitz wrote. "More intensive use of such techniques would probably damage monitorability."
 
[...] In a post responding to the news, Redwood Research chief scientist Ryan Greenblatt said opaque reasoning could easily scale faster than conventional chain-of-thought reasoning, effectively removing all reasoning from visible channels. "My biggest concern is that a natural progression from here would involve scaling up the opaque reasoning to the point where the model reasons entirely or almost entirely in latent space," Greenblatt wrote. "I hope it isn't too late to avoid the most concerning architectures and that OpenAI will stop here." Astra's use of the technique appears limited. "OpenAI has worked to preserve and utilize chain-of-thought monitoring since our very first reasoning models," wrote OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki. "It's a core goal of our current research program."

report.summary: OpenAI新模型Astra采用不透明推理技术引发AI安全专家担忧。
report.background: 近两年主流推理模型依赖“思维链”（Chain of Thought）——让模型把推理步骤显式写成文本，便于人类检查与监控。OpenAI计划在Astra模型中引入“循环深度”技术，使模型能在隐藏的循环或潜在空间中完成推理，而非逐步可见。这项技术被称为“不透明循环”，一旦规模扩大，传统思维链监控将失效。Redwood Research高管、AI安全倡导者等人均表示强烈担忧，认为这会引发实验室之间的“逐底竞争”，甚至需要法律约束。OpenAI回应称目前应用有限，并承诺继续以思维链可监控性为核心目标。
key_points: Astra将采用“循环深度”推理，模型可在不透明内部循环中思考，不再遵循可读的逐步思维链过程。
安全专家担心该技术会摧毁思维链的可监控性，让人类更难评估模型是否忠实、安全地推理。
研究者警告不透明推理扩展速度更快，若持续放大，模型可能在几乎不可见的“潜在空间”中完成全部推理。
OpenAI辩称当前使用范围有限，强调仍致力于思维链监控，但专家呼吁立法以防止AI实验室间安全标准下滑。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，这会加剧能力与可解释性之间的张力：模型可能在隐藏空间中获得更强推理能力，却失去人工审计窗口，监管部门将更难设定可验证的安全标准。对开发者来说，调试和对齐Astra这类模型会变得更复杂，错误行为可能难以定位。对普通用户，AI决策将更不透明，一旦出现有害输出，追责与纠错机制都会被削弱，公众信任可能进一步下降。
report.tools: 可关注OpenAI官方发布的技术报告与模型卡，了解其对思维链监控的说明；Anthropic的可解释性相关研究；Redwood Research关于思维链监控与对齐的开源报告，以及Neuronpedia等可解释性可视化工具。
